name: Komoot Premium
subcategory: trip planning, navigation and travel intelligence
tagline: Plan routes from open map data and export GPX files with clear data sources

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Worldwide route planning plus 1 Single Region unlocked forever for turn-by-turn navigation and offline maps

tiers.name: Single Region
tiers.limits: Permanent navigation and offline-map unlock for 1 region
tiers.notes: One-time regional price is location-dependent and was not published on the public page.

tiers.name: Region Bundle
tiers.limits: Permanent navigation and offline-map unlock for 1 multi-region bundle
tiers.notes: One-time bundle price is location-dependent and was not published on the public page.

tiers.name: World Pack
tiers.limits: Permanent worldwide voice navigation and offline maps
tiers.notes: $29.99 one-time; a $19.99 welcome offer may be shown to eligible accounts.

tiers.name: Premium
tiers.limits: Worldwide maps/navigation, multi-day planner, personal collections, live tracking, route weather, sport maps, 3D maps, and Garmin map
tiers.notes: $59.99 billed annually; exact price can vary by storefront and country.

tiers.name: Premium Family
tiers.limits: Family subscription exists; exact member cap and current USD billing periods were not exposed on the public pricing page
tiers.notes: Public App Store listings show multiple family offers, but their duration-to-price mapping could not be verified.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan: worldwide planning and 1 Single Region unlocked forever; navigation/offline maps outside that region require a one-time map purchase or Premium.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual Premium, one-time regional/world map purchases, and a separately sold Family plan
pricing.hiddenCosts: World Pack only unlocks maps/navigation and does not include Premium planning, weather, tracking, collection, or sport-map features. Storefront pricing and welcome offers vary.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Komoot Premium, plan routes from open map data and export GPX files with clear data sources. The hard boundary is routing profiles, regional maps, community highlights, navigation, and offline apps, plus proprietary live data and network coverage.
coreLoopDIY: Plan routes from open map data, export GPX files with clear data sources, map user-entered places, and keep an offline itinerary without claiming live proprietary availability.
requirements: optional public transit or weather API
whatYouLose: routing profiles, regional maps, community highlights, navigation, and offline apps
booking, disruption support, and offline map fleet
moatNotes: proprietary live data and network coverage
ongoingBurden: map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Komoot Premium because travel subscriptions sell current data and confidence during disruption, not just an itinerary list. The recurring cost buys map licensing, fare feeds, reservation access, route freshness, disruptions, geocoding, caching, offline data, and support, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Wanderer
priorArt.desc: Open-source self-hosted trail database and route explorer using open map data.

alternatives.name: OsmAnd~
alternatives.desc: The F-Droid build plans offline routes and handles GPX without paid region packs.

facts.install: Install the free OsmAnd~ APK from F-Droid and download the required offline regions
facts.dataFormat: Downloaded vector maps, routing indexes, settings, favorites, and recorded tracks live in the Android app's local storage; routes and tracks can be imported or exported as GPX, and optional user-configured backup/sync targets are separate from the F-Droid app itself.
facts.gapVsPaid: OsmAnd is exceptionally capable offline, but its dense controls, weaker community route discovery, less polished surface and difficulty guidance, and lower social-trip polish make planning harder than Komoot.
facts.setupBlocker: The first hurdle is installing through F-Droid rather than a normal paid-store purchase, then budgeting several gigabytes and time for offline map downloads.

alternatives.name: Organic Maps
alternatives.desc: Offline OSM routing and GPX import/export with no region packs to buy.

facts.install: Install from the mobile app store or F-Droid, then download map regions for offline use
facts.dataFormat: Offline vector map packages derived from OpenStreetMap live on the device; bookmarks and tracks live in the app's local profile and can be imported/exported in formats including KML/KMZ and GPX. Normal navigation does not require an Organic Maps account.
facts.gapVsPaid: Organic Maps handles simple offline routes, but it lacks Komoot's sport-specific profiles, elevation and surface analysis, curated highlights, community collections, and tour-planning depth.
facts.setupBlocker: There is no meaningful installation blocker beyond downloading regions, but storage use grows quickly and the route-planning controls are much less specialized for multi-day outdoor trips than Komoot's.

alternatives.name: Wanderer
alternatives.desc: Plan and catalogue OSM routes on your server, then export the GPX and own the maintenance too.

facts.dataFormat: Routes, lists, user records, and activity metadata live in the deployment's application database; imported GPX files, photos, and generated assets live in persistent Docker volumes, and routes remain exportable as GPX. Map tiles and routing data come from the configured external or self-hosted map services.
facts.gapVsPaid: Wanderer gives ownership of routes, but requires a server and does not match Komoot's mobile navigation polish, community recommendations, worldwide route intelligence, or automatic map updates.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must run a multi-container service with persistent storage, secrets, a domain/TLS, backups, and any required map-provider configuration before the route planner is reliably available away from home.

alternatives.name: gpx.studio
alternatives.desc: Plan and edit GPX routes in a browser; it saves files, not your travel life.

facts.install: Use the hosted browser/PWA, or self-host the static web application with Docker or a normal web build
facts.dataFormat: GPX tracks are parsed and edited in the browser and exported back to files on the user's device; the hosted service states that route files are not uploaded to its server, although map/routing providers still receive the network requests needed to draw and route the map.
facts.gapVsPaid: gpx.studio is an excellent GPX editor, not a full trip service: it lacks offline mobile navigation, saved-tour sync, sport-specific recommendations, highlights, live tracking, and community discovery.
facts.setupBlocker: The hosted editor has no setup blocker; the trade is that it is file-centric rather than an account-based trip library, so the user must organize, sync, and back up GPX files separately.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Premium plan and a personal itinerary organizer DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Komoot Premium in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, MapLibre GL, and user-supplied map and travel APIs; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: plan routes from open map data, export GPX files with clear data sources, map user-entered places, and keep an offline itinerary without claiming live proprietary availability.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create trips, days, places, reservations, notes, documents, packing items, and emergency contacts.
Geocode only user-entered places and display them through MapLibre with cached trip-area tiles where allowed.
Parse forwarded reservation text locally into editable fields without logging message content.
Build a day timeline, route overview, conflict warnings, timezone display, and offline printable itinerary.
Allow manual updates for delays and reservations and label all external data with source and timestamp.
Export a complete trip bundle as JSON, calendar file, Markdown, and PDF.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out live flight, hotel, award, or ticket inventory.
Deliberately leave out commercial turn-by-turn navigation and global offline maps.
Deliberately leave out booking guarantees, disruption rebooking, and traveler support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
